layout.title: 98″ corner TV · 6-seat L facing it
notes: The TV angles across the south-east corner on a 56″ corner console, so the main run and the return both face it: no seat looks away from the screen.
L sectional 44″ deep, 15″ off the west glass (room for shades). Main run 106″ (y 37–143) with two 29″ seats plus the corner; return 136″ (x 18–154) with three 29″ seats.
Seats sit 8½–14 ft from the screen, which fills 29–45° of view; four seats are prime, two are good.
Coffee table: Living Spaces Aries II cocktail ottoman, 66 × 27 × 18″, with the 30 × 24″ MAGIGO walnut tray (both from ideas/README.md), 16″ from both seat fronts.

findings: terra: the strongest balanced proposal; prefers it to G1 for the extra seat and larger sectional. Check the 56-inch pedestal stand rating and the TV end 11 inches in front of the south glass.
sonnet: no material change. The sofa corner sat 0.01 inch from the column; move the sofa 3 inches north (y 40-146) and keep 4 prime / 2 good with a 49-inch island aisle.
sonnet: rotating the TV and console to 310 makes seat 6 prime (5 prime / 1 good) but leaves the TV 1.6 inches from the south glass.
Notes said 8.5-14 ft and 15 inches off the glass; the measured values are 8 ft 0 in - 13 ft 6 in and 18 inches.

grok: the one point off is floor-plan adherence: the south edge is tangent to the column (0.0 inch, traced column). Move sofa, ottoman and rug 4 inches north: sofa (86, 94), ottoman (111, 73.5), rug (106, 95); 4.0 inch column gap, 48 inch island aisle, same seats.
outcome: Applied grok’s 4-inch shift as G2-final and sent it to all three reviewers for round 5.
